name: Django pickle session serializer
attack_scenario: An attacker who can write a crafted pickle into the session store (or forge one after a key leak) triggers __reduce__ on deserialization, running os.system('id')-style code in the web process.
negative_test_hint: write a crafted session payload whose pickle executes "os.system('id')" via __reduce__ and assert the session backend refuses to unpickle it and no command runs

exemplar.explanation: Setting SESSION_SERIALIZER to PickleSerializer makes Django unpickle session payloads. If an attacker can influence stored session data (via a separate SECRET_KEY leak, a writable cache/DB session backend, or any object-injection foothold) the unpickle executes attacker gadgets. This is distinct from the generic pickle.loads detector: it targets the Django session-backend config knob. Django ships JSONSerializer as the default precisely to remove this RCE surface; PickleSerializer was removed entirely in Django 5.1.
